M10.01.note: Approved narration uses at least three distinct P-wave morphologies in one lead, variable PR and an irregular slower rhythm; minor shape differences or artifact alone do not establish WAP. No verified WAP/MAT strip or shifting-focus model is supplied.

M10.02.note: The approved adaptation allows normally conducted, aberrant or blocked PACs rather than assuming normal narrow conduction in every premature atrial event. No PAC specimen or premature-beat simulation is supplied.

M10.03.note: Atrial and ventricular rates/conduction are distinguished. A source rate range or narrow QRS alone does not identify the exact mechanism. No focal-atrial-tachycardia specimen or rhythm engine is supplied.

M10.04.note: Typical flutter is explained as a large re-entry circuit, correcting the course single-irritable-focus shorthand. A source ECG can show atrial-wave morphology and ventricular regularity, but cannot establish a precise flutter subtype, circuit, atrial rate or conduction ratio.

M10.05.note: Approved narration distinguishes disorganized atrial activity, ventricular response and exceptions. The available source AF specimen has a slow response around 50 bpm. Baseline ripples do not justify a precise atrial rate; waveform appearance alone does not quantify an individual risk or treatment.

M10.06.note: Known flutter and AF teaching examples support feature comparison only. They are different source recordings, not a controlled regularity experiment; neither ventricular regularity nor irregularity alone proves the rhythm. No individual thromboembolic-risk or treatment assessment is performed.

M10.07.note: Learner-controlled, unrecorded and unscored description checkpoint. Only the existing flutter and AF specimens are available; WAP/MAT, PAC and focal-atrial-tachycardia examples are not invented.

verification.method: Independent visual inspection of extracted source waveform, approximate grid counts and atrial/ventricular relationships, then comparison with course context. Not a clinician sign-off.
